subject: Contract sequencing & uplift governance Q&A
summary: OptimaCloud asks for sequencing of signatures and proration mechanics for an upsell + 12-month term extension; internal legal proposes targeted redlines and asks for signatory order; customer confirms sign order and requests DocuSign envelope.
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@optimacloud.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: OptimaCloud Procurement <procurement@optimacloud.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract sequencing & uplift governance Q&A

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the call this morning — quick follow up from our procurement team as we review the SOW (attached). Two items they want clarified before we push the package to legal:

1) Signing order and sequencing: Optima prefers Purchase Order -> Sales signature -> Customer signature sequence, but our legal is asking if Redwood can do a combined MSA amendment + orderform bundle routed via DocuSign with the customer signing last. Do you have an advised sequence to avoid delays?

2) Billing/proration: We're upselling mid-cycle for a capacity uplift (extra GPU hours) and extending term +12 months. Procurement wants explicit proration language and an example calc for a Sept 15 start date.

3) Governance/redlines: attached SOW v3 has a couple of tracked changes from our side (mostly scope and service windows). Our legal flagged a data residency sentence in Section 7 of the MSA and wants to confirm Redwood's proposal for EU data-at-rest controls if we include that obligation in the order bundle.

Can you confirm who to loop from Redwood legal/finance and whether you can produce a single consolidated PDF (MSA excerpt + SOW + redline summary) for routing?

Thanks — would like to close this week if possible.

Best,
Megan
Megan Liu
Head of Procurement, OptimaCloud
megan.liu@optimacloud.com

Attachment: Optima_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@optimacloud.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract sequencing & uplift governance Q&A

Megan — thanks for the concise list. Quick answers and a proposed path: 

1) Signing sequence: we recommend (a) Redwood signs the orderform and any addenda first (internal sales exec + finance), (b) we upload consolidated bundle to DocuSign, and (c) Optima signs last. That keeps our internal PO processing and billing cutover aligned. If Optima prefers the PO first, we can accommodate but it sometimes delays our EPS/finance stamping.

2) Proration example: for a Sept 15 capacity uplift + term extension to run a 12-month renewal from Sept 15 — pro rata for the remainder of that billing month will be charged on the first invoice after signature; example calc attached in RDW_redlines_v1.docx (sample table). We'll include explicit language: "proration will be calculated on a pro rata daily basis for partial billing cycles".

3) Data residency: we can accept a scoped EU-at-rest obligation limited to customer data stored on dedicated instances (if dedicated selected). For hosted shared deployments we can offer contractual commitment to encrypt-at-rest in EU region + KMS controls; we cannot commit to on-prem unless pre-negotiated. Lauren/neha — can you review the proposed sentence below and apply to MSA Section 7 in the consolidated bundle?

Proposed MSA sentence (draft): "Where Customer elects a dedicated deployment or specifies regional residency in the Order, Redwood will ensure that Customer data at rest is stored in the specified region and will enable customer-managed KMS where requested and feasible. For shared-hosted deployments Redwood will maintain encryption at rest in the chosen region using provider KMS; Customer acknowledges that full physical control of infrastructure is not transferred."

Next steps: Lauren to produce tracked redline snippets for MSA Section 3 (Term), Section 5 (Billing/proration), and Section 7 (Data residency). Neha to confirm final billing example numbers. I can compile the consolidated PDF and push DocuSign envelope (we'll propose Redwood signs first then Optima last). If that works, I'll propose a DocuSign envelope id and circulate.

Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW_redlines_v1.docx (contains sample proration table and our suggested MSA sentence)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@optimacloud.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract sequencing & uplift governance Q&A

Looping in legal language here — Megan, thanks for raising Section 7. Couple of targeted edits below (we'll produce the tracked redline PDF by EOD):

- TERM (MSA Section 3): we propose a single-sentence addendum clarifying that any term extension triggered by an Order will supersede the original MSA term for the Order's services only. Suggested language: "Any term extension included in an Order will apply solely to the services described in that Order and will not modify other Orders unless explicitly stated."

- BILLING / PRORATION (MSA Section 5): replace vague references with explicit calc method: daily proration based on calendar days in the relevant billing month, rounding to the nearest cent; include example table in SOW appendix.

- DATA RESIDENCY (MSA Section 7): tweak Rishi's draft to limit obligations where Redwood uses third-party shared infrastructure. Proposed redline: "Subject to the service configuration selected in the Order, Redwood will (i) store Customer data at rest within the specified geographic region where Customer has ordered regional residency; (ii) enable customer-managed encryption keys for dedicated deployments; and (iii) for shared-hosted deployments use industry standard encryption and regional storage controls but will not be liable for physical infrastructure control."

We also suggest adding a small signatory governance clause to the orderform appendix that defines sign order if a customer PO is used. That clause reduces routing confusion in procurement-led customers.

I'll push tracked MSA excerpts + an annotated cover memo to the drive link Rishi provided and will flag any items that require finance approval (e.g., pro rata rounding rules).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_excerpt_section7.pdf (annotated excerpt)

From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@optimacloud.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, OptimaCloud Procurement <procurement@optimacloud.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract sequencing & uplift governance Q&A

Thanks Rishi & Lauren — that path is fine with us. A few quick confirmations so our legal can close their review: 

• Optima will sign last. We will attach our PO to the DocuSign envelope but we ask Redwood to be the first signer to ensure billing transition date aligns with your finance systems.

• Data residency language above is acceptable for our use case (we are pursuing dedicated instances for the uplift). Please make sure the consolidated PDF clearly flags the dedicated deployment assumption.

• Please include the proration example for Sept 15 in the PDF appendix with the math broken out (days/total days x uplift fee). Procurement will not accept ambiguous wording there.

If you can circulate the DocuSign envelope by EOD PDT with the consolidated PDF, we'll route internally and aim to sign within 48 hours. DocuSign envelope request: please set signer order: Redwood Sales (1) -> Redwood Finance (2) -> Optima Cloud (3).

Once we have the envelope id I'll confirm with procurement and legal. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Best,
Megan

DocuSign request link: https://docusign.example.com/request/EDU-1092387
